text:
MPC fell about 0.4% today as oil prices remained under pressure amid shifting geopolitical headlines. Over the past two trading days, the stock dropped roughly 5.5% after hitting $425 on September 18th—the steepest decline came Monday (September 21st) when crude tumbled below $100 a barrel on reports that Trump was open to talking with Iran, which eased some fears about supply disruptions from the Middle East. Today the stock continued lower even though oil prices barely moved, suggesting the market is still digesting the possibility of de-escalation in the Iran situation rather than reacting to fresh news.

Refineries are running at a robust 96.8% capacity with healthy product inventories, but that operational strength can't offset what's happening on the price side. With crude swinging between $100 and $107 per barrel depending on the day's geopolitical headlines, and Wall Street openly admitting uncertainty about oil's direction, refiner margins are caught between competing forces: lower crude prices help costs but also weaken the value of refined products, and the lack of clarity on Iran is keeping traders cautious.
